harness_retention.note: each rebuild cycle and lifecycle capture retains one MemoryCapturePoint (plus its capture-name string) inside this report; that harness retention is part of the measured live-allocator delta and is reconciled against the projection category sums

instrumentation.allocator_probe: replaced global operator new/delete: live+cumulative requested and usable bytes, allocation counts, live peak; C++ allocations only (SQLite C allocations are outside the counter)
instrumentation.process_memory: GetProcessMemoryInfo PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS_EX (working set, private usage, peak working set, peak pagefile)
instrumentation.working_set_split: QueryWorkingSet + QueryWorkingSetEx page classification (shareable vs private)
instrumentation.projection_categories: Projection::GetMemoryBreakdown live capacity/size/bucket_count measurements; modeled_category_bytes equals Projection::EstimatedMemoryBytes

limitations: allocator counts cover C++ operator new/delete only; SQLite (compiled as C) allocates through malloc/free and appears in the private-bytes residual instead
standard-library node links, the probe's 32-byte allocation header, heap block headers and heap rounding are residual and are not attributed to any projection category
working-set shareable pages identify shareable/pagefile-backed pages; they are not proof that another process maps the same section

the export weighing uses the real IndexPipeline pooled/owning export and SnapshotPublisher publish APIs in one process; the UI-side parse here is the in-process published-section read, not the FastFiles UI process
timings in this mode are single-process measurements and are not the campaign's idle-gated latency protocol
this executable replaces the global operator new/delete in every mode, so any other mode of this benchmark binary is instrumented and must not be used as uninstrumented latency evidence
all byte quantities are binary (MiB = 1048576 bytes); allocator counts exclude the C-only SQLite allocation plane
